---
title: "Backpropagation and Automatic Differentiation"
description: "An original worked mathematical lesson corresponding to MML §5.6."
---

**Reference:** *Mathematics for Machine Learning*, Chapter 5, §5.6. The teaching example and explanation here are original.

## Why we need this concept

Deep models compose many transformations. Backpropagation applies the chain rule backward through this computation graph without symbolically expanding the entire composition.

## Derive the structure

$$
\frac{\partial L}{\partial a}=\frac{\partial L}{\partial b}\frac{\partial b}{\partial a}
$$

Check the shapes and conditions in this statement before applying it. The formula encodes the exact relationship to reason about, rather than replacing a derivation with a library call.

## Worked example

Suppose a=2, b=3a=6 and L=(b-9)^2=9. First dL/db=2(b-9)=-6; then db/da=3, so dL/da=-18. Only local derivatives were needed.

## Interpretation and limitations

Reverse-mode automatic differentiation efficiently computes gradients of scalar loss with many parameters. It is not numerical finite differencing, and it requires a specified graph of differentiable operations.

## Challenge

For b=a^2 and L=(b-4)^2, derive dL/da at a=1 with the chain rule.
